About Us
Beaverlodge Funeral Service opened in November of 2012, in order to provide our local and rural communities with hometown service and an alternative choice.
By providing service with hometown people, we hope to make our families feel more comfortable and understood during their difficult time. All of us at Beaverlodge Funeral Service are dedicated to easing the burden of loss by offering support, guidance, and providing knowledgeable information.
We hope that you allow us to be there for you in your time of need.

window.getGAuuid = () => {
    const uuidKeyCookie = "tcouuid";
    const regexCookie = new RegExp(`(^| )${uuidKeyCookie}=([^;]+)`);
    const gaUUidCookieArr = document.cookie.match(regexCookie);
    if (!gaUUidCookieArr) {
        const now = new Date();
        let uuid = "crypto" in window && window.crypto.randomUUID && window.crypto.randomUUID();
        if (!uuid) {
            uuid = String(now.getTime().toString(32) + Math.random().toString(16)).replace(/\./g, '-');
        }
        now.setTime(now.getTime() + 3600 * 1000);// 1 hour
        document.cookie = `${uuidKeyCookie}=${uuid};expires=${now.toUTCString()};path=/`;
        return uuid;
    }
    return gaUUidCookieArr[2];
};

How to Select a Funeral Home
Choosing a funeral home is one of the most important decisions you will make during a difficult time. A funeral director coordinates countless details around the clock â our services are available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including holidays.
Before making the first call, consider: Do you know a funeral director's reputation in the community? Is the home locally owned? Does your family have past experience with them? Do they understand your religious, cultural, or personal needs?
We encourage families to visit, ask questions, and make sure they feel comfortable with the people guiding them. Pre-arranging is the best way to ensure your wishes are met and to relieve that burden from your family.

A Caring Cornerstone
of Your Community
The story of Cornerstone Funeral Home, serving Lethbridge & southern Alberta for three decades and three generations.
A Story That Reaches Back
Cornerstone Funeral Home was founded in 1995 by Ralph and Faith Zentner, but its roots reach back to a small town in Saskatchewan and a moment that would change one young manâs life forever.
Humboldt, Saskatchewan
The Early Years
Where the Story Begins
Ralph Zentner grew up in Humboldt, Saskatchewan, the youngest of six children in a hardworking family. At fourteen, Ralph lost a close friend in a snowmobile accident, a tragedy that shook their small community.
In the days that followed, he watched a local funeral director care for his friendâs family, and for the entire town, with such patience and compassion that it planted a seed that would shape the rest of his life. That summer, Ralph approached the funeral home and was told: finish school, then come see us.
Ralph Zentner, in the years before his lifeâs work began
Calgary
1982
Learning the Craft
After his family moved to Calgary and Ralph finished high school, he did exactly what he had been told to do, beginning an apprenticeship at McInnis & Holloway Funeral Homes in 1982.
His earliest days started, quite literally, from the ground up: washing and detailing the funeral homeâs fleet of cars by hand, polishing brass fixtures until they gleamed. It was humble work, but Ralph took real pride in it, and that pride in the details never left him. He trained under mentors like Peter Holakoff, whose photographic memory for every family he served left a lasting impression on what it truly means to care for people.
Licensed in 1984 with the highest marks in the province
September 1
1984
Ralph & Faith
It was at Chapel of the Bells that Ralph met Faith Oberhammer, who worked in the crematorium there. Edson Funeral Home & Foothills Crematorium is defined by the commitment and compassion of over 64 years of family service. We believe in personal attention and uncompromised quality. We are very proud of our traditions, facilities and the personal services that we provide.

We have the only crematorium in West Central Alberta, therefore there is no third party involvement and no extra mileage charges.

Please take the time you need to view how our services can address your funeral or cremation service needs. Whether your needs are immediate, or you are looking to pre-arrange services, we are ready to serve you with courtesy and respect during your time of need.

If you wish to discuss pre-arrangements, do not hesitate in calling us and we can arrange a meeting, in your home or at our office in either Edson or Hinton. We are available to assist without any obligation on your part.

About Us
Andy Dick
Funeral Director/Manager
Born in England in 1962, Andrew’s family
came to Canada in 1970. They made their first home in Grande Cache, but moved
to Edson in 1973. His first relationship with Foothills Memorial Chapel was
when he was 19 years old.  He serviced
cars and did general maintenance in and around the building. Soon he was asked
to make his first transfer from the hospital and he never looked back. In 1993
he was hired as a full time employee, shortly after he received his Funeral
Directors License. He moved to Trochu in 1997 to take over Prairie Winds
Funeral Home which he shortly after purchased and successfully owned until
2015. In quiet times,  he would still
travel to Edson to help out at the Foothills Memorial Chapel, Edson Funeral
Home throughout this time. After the sale of his own Funeral Home in Trochu his
stays in Edson became longer. When the Caring Group purchased the Funeral Home
he was asked to join the team on a full time basis and moved back to Edson. He
takes pride in caring for each family at a time making sure their needs are
met.
Email:
Kirsten Dick
Pre Arrangement Advisor / Office Administrator
Born
and raised in Germany, Kirsten came to Edson in 1982 to start a family. In 1998
she moved to Entwistle, Alberta where she started working for Servus Credit
Union in 2001. In 2002 she moved to Drayton Valley and continued working for
Servus Credit Union until 2016. That summer she decided to move back home to
Edson, where she started working as Funeral Attendant/ Office assistant at the
Foothills Memorial Chapel. Kirsten recently received her certification as a Pre Need Advisor. Kirsten enjoys the variety of duties in both
settings, especially when being able to assist families through a difficult
time. She is looking forward to finding out about different paths in this
industry and looks forward to serving your family.
Email:
Brandi Hudson
Funeral Director/ Embalmer
Brandi was born in Watson, Saskatchewan, but raised in the small secluded northern community of La Ronge, Saskatchewan. She moved out to Alberta at the age of 18 and over the years she has had few career changes but always found herself the happiest in health care and working closely with the elderly. In her free time, you’ll most likely find her with her two children and if it’s summer and the sun is shining, there’s a good chance there’s friends and fishing rods involved.
Brandi joined  the Edson Funeral Home back in December 2021 and enrolled into school the following year. She graduated from the two-year program at the Canadian College of Funeral Service in April 2024 and has enjoyed everything she has learned about the funeral service profession so far. She is very proud to have her Funeral Director and embalming licence and to be working closely with all the families.
Email:
Abby Dobbie
Apprentice Funeral Director
Born and raised in Edson, Abby first showed interest in the profession at the age of 14 when she came to the conclusion she wanted to help but had no desire to be a doctor or nurse. When she was 16, she joined her school’s work experience program for a few months to help decide if she really enjoyed the career. In the summer of 2025, she graduated from Parkland Composite High School and enrolled in college for the following school year. During this time, she began working at the Edson Funeral Home part-time, where she eventually transitioned into full-time. In her downtime Abby enjoys taking long walks around town and in the bush both alone and with her sister. She loves drawing, poetry, and looking after her aquariums. Abby is expected to graduate from Canadian College of Funeral Service by 2027 and earn her funeral directing and embalming license.
John Findlay
Funeral Attendant
John was born and raised in Edson. He enjoys being a part of the community. John started working with Foothills Memorial Funeral Home in 2017 as Funeral
Attendant he enjoys being there for families in their time of need on a part time basis.
Our History
The history of funeral service in Edson and area dates back to 1913 when a flu epidemic swept the area. The local hospital hired a townsperson to bury the victims of the epidemic.
More formally, The Edson Funeral Parlor started business in the years that followed and was known by that name until Liberty and Anne Joy purchased the business from the local owner. The business was then known as, The Edson Funeral Home. In about 1955, Liberty and Anne Joy partnered with Connelly-McKinley Funeral Home of Edmonton and operated as Connelly-McKinley Edson Funeral Home until 1978. In 1978, Anne Joy died and Liberty Joy dissolved the partnership with Connelly-McKinley.
Edson Funeral Home (The Foothills Memorial Chapel),
as it is now known, opened for business on January 1st, 1979 with Robert and Marilynn Joy.
Liberty Joy died in 1981
after serving Edson and area for more than thirty years in the funeral business.
Liberty and Anne Joy
Robert Joy
Marilynn Joy

About Us
We're honoured to serve our community
The caring and experienced professionals at
Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel
are here to support you through this difficult time. We offer a range of personalized services to suit your family’s wishes and requirements. You can count on us to help you plan a personal, lasting tribute to your loved one. And we’ll carefully guide you through the many decisions that must be made during this challenging time.
You are welcome to call us at any time of the day, any day of the week, for immediate assistance. Or, visit our funeral home in person at your convenience. We also provide a wealth of information here on our web site so you can learn more from the privacy of your own home.
We are a work family here to serve
In this difficult time, let our family help yours. Learn more about who we are and what we do in the bios below. Our team is comprised of dedicated and licensed professionals with the experience to answer all your questions regarding our services.
Please feel free to contact any of our team members at any time.
Leanne Young
Funeral Director/Business Manager
As a young entrepreneur, Leanne
co-founded Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel with her sister, Larissa in 2010,
driven by a deep desire to serve families with compassion and care. Now
managing the funeral home while Larissa has stepped away to focus on family,
she remains committed to providing a comforting and supportive space for those
navigating loss.
With over 15 years of experience
guiding families through one of life’s most difficult transitions, Leanne
understands that every farewell is personal and unique. She takes great care in
helping families honor their loved ones with dignity and meaning, ensuring
every service reflects the life and legacy being remembered.
Leanne lives in St. Paul with her husband Joe and is proud of her young adult
children Milana and Kaysen who are following their dreams.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Larissa Sadlowski
Funeral Director/Embalmer
Larissa Sadlowski (nee Buryn) was
born and raised in St. Paul.  She began her career in Funeral Service in
2005 at Yewchin’s Funeral Chapel, earning her Funeral Director & Embalmer’s
license apprenticing under John Yewchin.  Over the past 20 years, Larissa
has proudly served her community with commitment, kindness and compassion.
She and her husband Jamie
welcomed their first daughter Renn in September of 2023 and are anxiously
awaiting the arrival of their second child, due in July of 2025.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Melanie Goulet
Office Administrator/Apprentice Funeral Director
Melanie Goulet was born and raised in
the Lakeland area, where her love for music initially connected her to the
funeral industry at a young age. In December 2011, she discovered her passion
for serving families during their most difficult times. Melanie and her
husband, Robert, have a blended family with seven children. She is currently
pursuing her diploma in Funeral Directing, eager to continue growing in her
career and making a meaningful impact in her community. Her compassion and
commitment to serving families make her a valued member of our team.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Lorne Buryn
Funeral Attendant/Maintenance
Lorne has supported his girls, Leanne and Larissa, as they pursued their business goals from day 1. First, by being an unconditionally loving dad and secondly by being their business mentor and leader. He has worked along side the girls since they opened the funeral home in 2010 and is honoured to serve the community as a family. Now he enjoys semi-retirement spending the winter months in Arizona but continues to be a valued team member at the funeral home.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Melissa Crawford
Funeral Director/Embalmer
Melissa Crawford was born in Foxwarren, Manitoba, and moved to Alberta with her family in 1998. Her interest in funeral service began in Grade 8 and grew through a Grade 12 work placement at a Manitoba funeral home. In 2012, she decided to pursue a career in funeral service.
Melissa joined Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel in 2014 as an Apprentice Funeral Director and Embalmer. She earned her Funeral Director’s License in 2016 and her Embalmer’s License in 2017. Since then, she has been privileged to support families with compassion and respect during difficult times. Melissa takes great pride in her work and is dedicated to providing meaningful, professional care to every family she serves.
Outside of work, Melissa enjoys camping, fishing, and exploring the mountains with her partner, Jeff. She is also the proud mother of four children: Drevan, Derian, Avery, and Aryssa.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Jordan Hunt
Funeral Director/Embalmer
Jordan, originally from Dublin, Ireland, began her career in funeral service by earning her funeral directing and embalming licence in Barcelona, Spain. Working in the profession abroad gave her a unique, multicultural perspective on death care and the importance of honouring diverse traditions and grieving practices. Seeking to continue her professional journey in Canada, she relocated to Lethbridge, Alberta, where she enrolled at the Canadian College of Funeral Service to complete her Canadian licensing requirements. She is proud to have graduated as Valedictorian in April 2026.
Over the past two years, Jordan has compassionately served families in Lethbridge and the surrounding communities, guiding them through some of life’s most difficult moments with empathy, professionalism, and respect. She is passionate about helping families create meaningful, personalized tributes that reflect the lives and legacies of their loved ones, and strongly believes in the value of time, care, and dignity in the grieving process.
Jordan recently moved to St. Paul with her husband, Richard, and their three cats. She is honoured to continue serving her new community and is committed to providing thoughtful and attentive care to every family she works with.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
Richard Williams
Apprentice Funeral Director/Embalmer
Richard Williams, originally from Raymond, Alberta, spent a decade working in the oilfield before choosing to follow a more service-oriented path in funeral care. Growing up in a close-knit southern Alberta community shaped his values of hard work, respect, and helping others.
He is currently attending the Canadian College of Funeral Services, with plans to graduate in 2027. Richard is passionate about providing compassionate, dignified care and helping families navigate loss with understanding and support.
He works alongside his wife, Jordan Hunt, and is honoured to serve his community during times when care matters most.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:
John Yewchin
Funeral Director/Embalmer
John was born and raised in the small community of Elk Point. He graduated from the Alberta School of Mortuary Science in 1969, and after working in funeral homes in Edmonton, AB and Dawson Creek, BC, he moved to St. Paul in 1972. In 1980, John realized his dream and built and operated Yewchin’s Funeral Chapel where he served St. Paul and area families with care and compassion for over 30 years. John is semi-retired, and when time permits, still enjoys helping families at Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel.
Telephone:
1-780-645-2677
Email:

In December 2011, she discovered her passion for serving families during their most difficult times. Melanie and her husband, Robert, have a blended family with seven children. She is currently pursuing her diploma in Funeral Directing, eager to continue growing in her career and making a meaningful impact in her community. Her compassion and commitment to serving families make her a valued member of our team.


Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email: 

Lorne Buryn

Funeral Attendant/Maintenance

Lorne has supported his girls, Leanne and Larissa, as they pursued their business goals from day 1. First, by being an unconditionally loving dad and secondly by being their business mentor and leader. He has worked along side the girls since they opened the funeral home in 2010 and is honoured to serve the community as a family. Now he enjoys semi-retirement spending the winter months in Arizona but continues to be a valued team member at the funeral home.

Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email: 

Melissa Crawford

Funeral Director/Embalmer

Melissa Crawford was born in Foxwarren, Manitoba, and moved to Alberta with her family in 1998. Her interest in funeral service began in Grade 8 and grew through a Grade 12 work placement at a Manitoba funeral home. In 2012, she decided to pursue a career in funeral service.


Melissa joined Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel in 2014 as an Apprentice Funeral Director and Embalmer. She earned her Funeral Director’s License in 2016 and her Embalmer’s License in 2017. Since then, she has been privileged to support families with compassion and respect during difficult times. Melissa takes great pride in her work and is dedicated to providing meaningful, professional care to every family she serves.


Outside of work, Melissa enjoys camping, fishing, and exploring the mountains with her partner, Jeff. She is also the proud mother of four children: Drevan, Derian, Avery, and Aryssa.


Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email: 

Jordan Hunt

Funeral Director/Embalmer

Jordan, originally from Dublin, Ireland, began her career in funeral service by earning her funeral directing and embalming licence in Barcelona, Spain. Working in the profession abroad gave her a unique, multicultural perspective on death care and the importance of honouring diverse traditions and grieving practices. Seeking to continue her professional journey in Canada, she relocated to Lethbridge, Alberta, where she enrolled at the Canadian College of Funeral Service to complete her Canadian licensing requirements. She is proud to have graduated as Valedictorian in April 2026.

Over the past two years, Jordan has compassionately served families in Lethbridge and the surrounding communities, guiding them through some of life’s most difficult moments with empathy, professionalism, and respect. She is passionate about helping families create meaningful, personalized tributes that reflect the lives and legacies of their loved ones, and strongly believes in the value of time, care, and dignity in the grieving process.

Jordan recently moved to St. Paul with her husband, Richard, and their three cats. She is honoured to continue serving her new community and is committed to providing thoughtful and attentive care to every family she works with.

Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email: 

Richard Williams

Apprentice Funeral Director/Embalmer

Richard Williams, originally from Raymond, Alberta, spent a decade working in the oilfield before choosing to follow a more service-oriented path in funeral care. Growing up in a close-knit southern Alberta community shaped his values of hard work, respect, and helping others.

He is currently attending the Canadian College of Funeral Services, with plans to graduate in 2027. Richard is passionate about providing compassionate, dignified care and helping families navigate loss with understanding and support.

He works alongside his wife, Jordan Hunt, and is honoured to serve his community during times when care matters most.

Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email: 

John Yewchin

Funeral Director/Embalmer

John was born and raised in the small community of Elk Point. He graduated from the Alberta School of Mortuary Science in 1969, and after working in funeral homes in Edmonton, AB and Dawson Creek, BC, he moved to St. Paul in 1972. In 1980, John realized his dream and built and operated Yewchin’s Funeral Chapel where he served St. Paul and area families with care and compassion for over 30 years. John is semi-retired, and when time permits, still enjoys helping families at Grace Gardens Funeral Chapel.

Telephone: 1-780-645-2677

Email:

Grace Memorial was very compassionate & professional in all aspects of the many details when we lost Wes. They were called very early in the morning and were ready for the family by late afternoon. Brian & Keri answered all our questions & explained everything regarding the paperwork to us. This made a very sad situation a little more comfortable. I have told everyone that I highly recommend them if they are in need of a funeral home.
Thank you Grace Memorial  - our family appreciates you more than we can express. 💜
Deb Kopp
10/30/2024

Our staff of dedicated professionals is available to assist you in making funeral service arrangements. From casket choices to funeral flowers, we will guide you through all aspects of the funeral service.
We invite you to contact us with your questions, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

Privacy Policy
Brian Redpath, Lorinda Unvoas, and Keri Seffern are proud to provide Medicine Hat and surrounding area with an affordable option. Together we have over 35 years experience in the funeral profession. Our goal is to provide the families we serve with modern service and traditional honourability while offering modest, package pricing. We are proud to offer our families and staff the highest level of mental wellness support.
Our Commitment
We are committed to providing quality care for the entire duration of your needs.
Pre – Needs
–    Pre-arranging your own service will help to ease the burden of your loved ones.  It will also alleviate any questions, problems or differences, which can occur among family members.
At – Needs
– Making funeral arrangements at the time death has occurred.
At Grace Memorial, the funeral profession is not a job.  It is a passion and a commitment to gaining the trust of you and your family.
Our Service
At Grace Memorial, we embrace traditional values, diversity, and modern innovation in honouring every family we serve.
We offer full traditional burial to simple cremation, with each family receiving personalized care.
Our prices are consistent regardless of the hour or day of the week our services are required.
When you choose Grace Memorial, you experience the dedication, knowledge and passion at the highest standard of service provided by our staff, who are owners/operators, in your time of need.
The caring and experienced professionals at
Grace Memorial Ltd. O/A Grace Memorial Affordable Burial & Cremation
are here to support you through this difficult time.  We offer a range of personalized services to suit your family’s wishes and requirements.  You can count on us to help you plan a personal, lasting tribute to your loved one.  And we’ll carefully guide you through the many decisions that must be made during this challenging time.
You are welcome to call us at any time of the day, any day of the week, for immediate assistance.  Or, visit our funeral home in person at your convenience.  We also provide a wealth of information here on our website so you can learn more from the privacy of your own home.

Privacy Policy
Brian Redpath, Lorinda Unvoas, and Keri Seffern are proud to provide Medicine Hat and surrounding area with an affordable option. Together we have over 35 years experience in the funeral profession. Our goal is to provide the families we serve with modern service and traditional honourability while offering modest, package pricing. We are proud to offer our families and staff the highest level of mental wellness support.
Our Commitment
We are committed to providing quality care for the entire duration of your needs.
Pre – Needs
–    Pre-arranging your own service will help to ease the burden of your loved ones.  It will also alleviate any questions, problems or differences, which can occur among family members.
At – Needs
– Making funeral arrangements at the time death has occurred.
At Grace Memorial, the funeral profession is not a job.  It is a passion and a commitment to gaining the trust of you and your family.
Our Service
At Grace Memorial, we embrace traditional values, diversity, and modern innovation in honouring every family we serve.
We offer full traditional burial to simple cremation, with each family receiving personalized care.
Our prices are consistent regardless of the hour or day of the week our services are required.
When you choose Grace Memorial, you experience the dedication, knowledge and passion at the highest standard of service provided by our staff, who are owners/operators, in your time of need.
The caring and experienced professionals at
Grace Memorial Ltd. O/A Grace Memorial Affordable Burial & Cremation
are here to support you through this difficult time.  We offer a range of personalized services to suit your family’s wishes and requirements.  You can count on us to help you plan a personal, lasting tribute to your loved one.  And we’ll carefully guide you through the many decisions that must be made during this challenging time.
You are welcome to call us at any time of the day, any day of the week, for immediate assistance.  Or, visit our funeral home in person at your convenience.  We also provide a wealth of information here on our website so you can learn more from the privacy of your own home.

Pre-Planning Options
Taking the time to arrange your funeral now leaves less details that your loved ones will need to worry about once you’ve passed. We are here to help you every step of the way.
While people spend months planning events like weddings and trips, few think about the one event that is certain to happen: their funeral.  While most people do not want to think about their own mortality, the time to pre-plan your funeral is now.  The primary advantage of pre-arranging your funeral is to relieve the burden on your loved ones in an emotional time, and to ensure your funeral is carried out according to your wishes, eliminating the task of second-guessing what you would have wanted. Pre-planning and pre-paying your funeral is one of the most thoughtful gifts you can give to your family.
WHAT YOU CAN DO IN ADVANCE…
Decide on Burial or Cremation options and your casket/urn.
Complete details for a personalized service that is appropriate for you and your family.
BENEFITS OF PRE-PLANNING
Between 70 and 75 decisions are made within the first 24-48 hours of death.  It’s difficult to think rationally while making so many decisions within days of losing someone. Pre-planning gives yourself, family, and friends peace of mind.
It’s easy. Anyone can do it, and you can change your mind at any time.
For more information surrounding the process of preplanning your funeral wishes, please Contact Us directly or fill out the form below.
CANADA PURPLE SHIELD & ASSURANT LIFE OF CANADA
Gregory’s Funeral Home has an established relationship of trust and integrity with Canada Purple Shield and Assurant Life of Canada. If you are more comfortable starting this conversation with Canada Purple Shield directly, please follow this link:

    const regexCookie = new RegExp(`(^| )${uuidKeyCookie}=([^;]+)`);
    const gaUUidCookieArr = document.cookie.match(regexCookie);
    if (!gaUUidCookieArr) {
        const now = new Date();
        let uuid = "crypto" in window && window.crypto.randomUUID && window.crypto.randomUUID();
        if (!uuid) {
            uuid = String(now.getTime().toString(32) + Math.random().toString(16)).replace(/\./g, '-');
        }
        now.setTime(now.getTime() + 3600 * 1000);// 1 hour
        document.cookie = `${uuidKeyCookie}=${uuid};expires=${now.toUTCString()};path=/`;
        return uuid;
    }
    return gaUUidCookieArr[2];
};

Quality Assurance
From End to End
From receiving trucks to making deliveries, Martin Bros. takes the same dedicated approach to maintaining product at the highest quality and safety.
Quality Inspectors
Our quality inspectors help maintain high standards of produce quality and food safety, giving fresh products extra time and attention. They also oversee First In, First Out rotation with inventory teams to support consistent quality.
Receiving & Delivery
All inbound loads are inspected before receiving, with temperatures checked during unloading using RF-based tools. Cold items move through refrigerated docks, and trained delivery personnel monitor trailer temperatures throughout each route.
Warehouse Cleanliness
Our distribution facility is cleaned monthly as part of our HACCP food safety program, and the warehouse team takes pride in a clean, well-organized environment. This commitment helped earn a 2025 GMP Food Safety audit score of 99.47% and an âexcellentâ rating.
Storage Temps
All products are stored according to food safety guidelines and Martin Bros. HACCP procedures, with defined conditions for dry, refrigerated, and frozen items. Computer systems continuously monitor each storage zone to verify proper temperature ranges.
Selecting Products
During order selection, products are picked in their appropriate storage zones and moved quickly through refrigerated, computer-monitored docks. Items are loaded into the correct temperature zone on the delivery trailer, with sensitive produce wrapped in thermal blankets during cold winter months.
Food Safety In Action
Listen as Jasna Sakanovic describes her role to inspect produce items daily, ensuring the freshest product is on hand and customers will have items that will last days after delivery. Her attention to detail is part of Martin Bros.â promise to provide legendary customer service.

David L. McCaw, Licensed Director
Dave started working for his brother Mert in 1953/54 while attending school in Turtleford. In 1956, Dave came to work for Mert full time, receiving his Saskatchewan embalmer's licence in 1958. He worked with Mert's widow, Helen until he purchased the business from her in 1964.
Dave married Agnes Johnson of the Turtleford area in 1958. Agnes was involved in all areas of the family business until her death in December of 1991. Dave and Agnes have five sons: Reg of Edmonton; Mark of Cochrane; Glenn of Lloydminster; Kurt of Calgary; and Dale who was tragically killed in a motor vehicle accident in 2009.
In April 2026, Dave was recognized by the Alberta Funeral Service Association (AFSA) for his 70 years of continuous service, not only to the profession but his community as well.

10 Facts about Grief and Grieving
By Dr Bill Webster
One reason that we often find grief such a difficult challenge is that we have never learned what to expect. The following facts will help you understand some crucial truths about grief and grieving and how we can work through the process to find healing.
1.  Grief is normal.
Grief is not a disease. It is the normal, human response to a significant loss.  People may encourage you to “be strong” or “not to cry”.  But how sad it would be if someone we cared about died and we didn’t cry or we carried on as if nothing had happened.  I’d like to think that someone will miss me enough to shed a tear after I’m gone.  Wouldn’t you?  When you lose someone special from your life you are going to grieve.  Our grief is saying that we miss the person and that we’re struggling to adjust to a life without that special relationship.  Admittedly, saying that grief is NORMAL does not minimize it’s DIFFICULTY.  It may be one of the most challenging experiences of your life.  But you are not crazy, or weak, or “not handling things”.  You are experiencing grief and after a significant loss that is a normal response.
2.  The worst kind of grief is YOURS
A loss is a very personal matter.  Your loss seems like the worst possible thing that could have happened to you.  Sometimes people ask if it is more difficult to lose a spouse than to lose a child.  Others question if it is worse to lose someone after a long lingering illness or if they die suddenly and unexpectedly from a heart attack or in an accident.  While these circumstances make each loss different, they are not important to you right now.  The worst kind of loss is yours.  When you lose a significant person from your life, whatever the relationship, it hurts and nothing takes away from your right to feel the loss and grief the absence of that person from your life.
3.  The way out of grief is through it.
Grief is painful.  Loss is one of the most difficult human experiences.  There is no easy way around it.  We may try to avoid the pain.  We may attempt to get over it as quickly as possible.  But most often it simply does not work that way.  Helen Keller said “The only way to get to the other side is to go through the door”.  We need to find the courage to go through this experience of grief.  Learning this is a major key to recovery.
4.  Your grief is intimately connected to the relationship
Every relationship holds a special and unique significance to us.  To fully interpret our grief response we need to understand what the relationship brought to my life and therefore what has been lost from my life.  We may grieve the loss of a parent differently from the loss of a friend.  Each made a different contribution to our lives.  What we have lost is not the same and so we grieve differently.  Two individuals, both experiencing the loss of a spouse, may grieve quite differently because of the differing circumstances (the duration, level of happiness, etc) of the relationship.
5.  Grief is hard work
A grief response is often referred to as “Grief-work”.  It requires more energy to work through than most people expect.  It takes a toll on us physically and emotionally.  This is why we often feel so fatigued after a loss, or why we may feel very apathetic towards people and events.  The problem is often compounded by people’s expectations of us to be strong or pull ourselves together or to get on with life.
6.  Your grief will take longer than most people think
How long will grief last?  It is finished when it is finished.  The first few months may be particularly intense.  The first year is difficult: especially the first Christmas, the first birthday, anniversary, Mother’s Day, Valentine’s Day, “a year ago today day” and many other times that remind us of our loss.  All are difficult days and we need to anticipate them, know they are normal and be compassionate with ourselves.    Some writers describe the  second year of grief as the lonely year when the realization of the life without the deceased becomes even more of a reality.  Take your time.  As John Donne says “He who has no time to mourn, has no time to mend.”  Grief always takes longer than people expect.
7.  Grief is unpredictable
You may experience a wide variety of feelings and reactions, not just those generally associated with grief, like sadness, crying, depression, etc.  Some of your responses may seem quite uncharacteristic.   “This isn’t like me,” you may think.  Grief is unpredictable.  We cannot present it in a neat predictable package.  Just when you think you have it figured out something comes along to surprise us.  In an unexpected moment, suddenly, without warning you find yourself missing the person again.  In fact the one predictable thing about grief is that it is unpredictable.
8.  There may be “Secondary losses” to deal with.
The death of any individual, difficult as that may be by itself, may also precipitate many other changes in your life.  For some it may mean the loss of financial security, a home, or even their independence.  For some it may mean the loss of a role:  (ex.)  the role of being a parent to a child who dies.  For others it may be the loss of our hopes and dreams of “living happily ever after” or enjoying retirement together, or having dad walk me down the aisle.  There may be many losses - environment, status, alteration of relationships - because of the death.  Each one has it’s own impact and each loss needs to be mourned.
9.  Grief comes and goes
We have said that grief is not a disease.  If you have a sore throat, it is painful for a few days, then the pain eases off and gradually disappears.  Grief does not work that way, however. Our healing process is different from a sickness model.   Sometimes, at first, we do not feel the pain of grief because we are in shock and numb.  Often the pain is more intense some months after the event.  Even then, grief is not unlike a roller coaster.  One day we feel pretty good, the next we find ourselves in the depths of despair.  Just when we think we are getting over it we may experience another devastating setback.  This can be discouraging to those who do not know what is happening.  Most have not learned that grief comes and goes and takes much longer than most people expect.  We need to realize that this is the way grief works itself out and trust that the process, difficult as it is, is helping us work towards reconciliation.
10.  Effective grief work is not done alone
Society has unrealistic expectations about mourning and often responds inappropriately.  Most people do not understand what is normal in grief, expecting us to get over it quickly and expressing these expectations in a way that seems less than sensitive.   Many people mistakenly believe that grief is so personal we want to keep it to ourselves.  People mean well, but they are not being helpful.  Sometimes when people are using cliches or expressing unrealistic expectations we feel like shutting ourselves away.  Often they feel uncomfortable with our grief and so, shortly after the funeral is over, the person or the loss is not mentioned.  There sometimes seems to be a conspiracy of silence.  People are afraid to say or do the wrong thing so they say and do nothing which is possibly the worst thing.  Grieving people need to talk.  Not everyone will be willing or even able to respond to you.  In fairness, not everyone can.  Accept that and try to find a support group or a counsellor who can help, or talk to someone who has been through a similar experience.  I believe in the power of shared experiences, and often others who have been through the deep places can be a real help.  Grief is about coping with the loss of a relationship and often in a helping relationship, relief can be found.

10 Facts about Grief and Grieving

By Dr Bill Webster

One reason that we often find grief such a difficult challenge is that we have never learned what to expect. The following facts will help you understand some crucial truths about grief and grieving and how we can work through the process to find healing.

    1.  Grief is normal.

Grief is not a disease. It is the normal, human response to a significant loss.  People may encourage you to “be strong” or “not to cry”.  But how sad it would be if someone we cared about died and we didn’t cry or we carried on as if nothing had happened.  I’d like to think that someone will miss me enough to shed a tear after I’m gone.  Wouldn’t you?  When you lose someone special from your life you are going to grieve.  Our grief is saying that we miss the person and that we’re struggling to adjust to a life without that special relationship.  Admittedly, saying that grief is NORMAL does not minimize it’s DIFFICULTY.  It may be one of the most challenging experiences of your life.  But you are not crazy, or weak, or “not handling things”.  You are experiencing grief and after a significant loss that is a normal response. 

     2.  The worst kind of grief is YOURS

A loss is a very personal matter.  Your loss seems like the worst possible thing that could have happened to you.  Sometimes people ask if it is more difficult to lose a spouse than to lose a child.  Others question if it is worse to lose someone after a long lingering illness or if they die suddenly and unexpectedly from a heart attack or in an accident.  While these circumstances make each loss different, they are not important to you right now.  The worst kind of loss is yours.  When you lose a significant person from your life, whatever the relationship, it hurts and nothing takes away from your right to feel the loss and grief the absence of that person from your life. 

    3.  The way out of grief is through it.

Grief is painful.  Loss is one of the most difficult human experiences.  There is no easy way around it.  We may try to avoid the pain.  We may attempt to get over it as quickly as possible.  But most often it simply does not work that way.  Helen Keller said “The only way to get to the other side is to go through the door”.  We need to find the courage to go through this experience of grief.  Learning this is a major key to recovery. 

    4.  Your grief is intimately connected to the relationship

Every relationship holds a special and unique significance to us.  To fully interpret our grief response we need to understand what the relationship brought to my life and therefore what has been lost from my life.  We may grieve the loss of a parent differently from the loss of a friend.  Each made a different contribution to our lives.  What we have lost is not the same and so we grieve differently.  Two individuals, both experiencing the loss of a spouse, may grieve quite differently because of the differing circumstances (the duration, level of happiness, etc) of the relationship. 

    5.  Grief is hard work

A grief response is often referred to as “Grief-work”.  It requires more energy to work through than most people expect.  It takes a toll on us physically and emotionally.  This is why we often feel so fatigued after a loss, or why we may feel very apathetic towards people and events.  The problem is often compounded by people’s expectations of us to be strong or pull ourselves together or to get on with life. 

    6.  Your grief will take longer than most people think

How long will grief last?  It is finished when it is finished.  The first few months may be particularly intense.  The first year is difficult: especially the first Christmas, the first birthday, anniversary, Mother’s Day, Valentine’s Day, “a year ago today day” and many other times that remind us of our loss.  All are difficult days and we need to anticipate them, know they are normal and be compassionate with ourselves.    Some writers describe the  second year of grief as the lonely year when the realization of the life without the deceased becomes even more of a reality.  Take your time.  As John Donne says “He who has no time to mourn, has no time to mend.”  Grief always takes longer than people expect. 

     7.  Grief is unpredictable

You may experience a wide variety of feelings and reactions, not just those generally associated with grief, like sadness, crying, depression, etc.  Some of your responses may seem quite uncharacteristic.   “This isn’t like me,” you may think.  Grief is unpredictable.  We cannot present it in a neat predictable package.  Just when you think you have it figured out something comes along to surprise us.  In an unexpected moment, suddenly, without warning you find yourself missing the person again.  In fact the one predictable thing about grief is that it is unpredictable.

     8.  There may be “Secondary losses” to deal with.

The death of any individual, difficult as that may be by itself, may also precipitate many other changes in your life.  For some it may mean the loss of financial security, a home, or even their independence.  For some it may mean the loss of a role:  (ex.)  the role of being a parent to a child who dies.  For others it may be the loss of our hopes and dreams of “living happily ever after” or enjoying retirement together, or having dad walk me down the aisle.  There may be many losses - environment, status, alteration of relationships - because of the death.  Each one has it’s own impact and each loss needs to be mourned.

    9.  Grief comes and goes

We have said that grief is not a disease.  If you have a sore throat, it is painful for a few days, then the pain eases off and gradually disappears.  Grief does not work that way, however. Our healing process is different from a sickness model.   Sometimes, at first, we do not feel the pain of grief because we are in shock and numb.  Often the pain is more intense some months after the event.  Even then, grief is not unlike a roller coaster.  One day we feel pretty good, the next we find ourselves in the depths of despair.  Just when we think we are getting over it we may experience another devastating setback.  This can be discouraging to those who do not know what is happening.  Most have not learned that grief comes and goes and takes much longer than most people expect.  We need to realize that this is the way grief works itself out and trust that the process, difficult as it is, is helping us work towards reconciliation. 

    10.  Effective grief work is not done alone

Society has unrealistic expectations about mourning and often responds inappropriately.  Most people do not understand what is normal in grief, expecting us to get over it quickly and expressing these expectations in a way that seems less than sensitive.   Many people mistakenly believe that grief is so personal we want to keep it to ourselves.  People mean well, but they are not being helpful.  Sometimes when people are using cliches or expressing unrealistic expectations we feel like shutting ourselves away.  Often they feel uncomfortable with our grief and so, shortly after the funeral is over, the person or the loss is not mentioned.  There sometimes seems to be a conspiracy of silence.  People are afraid to say or do the wrong thing so they say and do nothing which is possibly the worst thing.  Grieving people need to talk.  Not everyone will be willing or even able to respond to you.  In fairness, not everyone can.  Accept that and try to find a support group or a counsellor who can help, or talk to someone who has been through a similar experience.  I believe in the power of shared experiences, and often others who have been through the deep places can be a real help.  Grief is about coping with the loss of a relationship and often in a helping relationship, relief can be found.

About Us
Mission View Funeral Chapel Ltd. was established in 1992 by Derrick Kruk. In 1996 he married Nola and together they served the Lac La Biche area for over 25 years. In November 2017, Jeff and Teresa Thackeray were honored to take over the well established business and continue to serve the area.
Jeff and Teresa currently reside in Bonnyville, they have 2 children, Sydney and Scott. Together they also, own and operate Memento Funeral Chapel, a family run business since 1975 when Jeff's parents, Don and Elda Thackeray purchased it. In fact, Derrick once lived in Bonnyville and was employed by Don in the mid 1980's. It's kind of interesting how things turn out!
The Alberta Funeral Service Association honored four of our staff with long standing awards, Don with his 50th, Elda with her 40th, Derrick with his 35th and Jeff with his 25th year award for their service and dedication in the funeral industry. Together, with our team, we will continue to strive to serve all communities with outmost respect and dignity.

About Us
Mission View Funeral Chapel Ltd. was established in 1992 by Derrick Kruk. In 1996 he married Nola and together they served the Lac La Biche area for over 25 years. In November 2017, Jeff and Teresa Thackeray were honored to take over the well established business and continue to serve the area.
Jeff and Teresa currently reside in Bonnyville, they have 2 children, Sydney and Scott. Together they also, own and operate Memento Funeral Chapel, a family run business since 1975 when Jeff's parents, Don and Elda Thackeray purchased it. In fact, Derrick once lived in Bonnyville and was employed by Don in the mid 1980's. It's kind of interesting how things turn out!
The Alberta Funeral Service Association honored four of our staff with long standing awards, Don with his 50th, Elda with her 40th, Derrick with his 35th and Jeff with his 25th year award for their service and dedication in the funeral industry. Together, with our team, we will continue to strive to serve all communities with outmost respect and dignity.

Testimonials of Our Care
"We had nothing but exemplary, compassionate service and guidance from Park Memorial and their staff"
"While my Mother didn't pass away unexpectedly, her end came much more quickly than was expected. We had nothing but exemplary, compassionate service and guidance from Park Memorial (Edmonton) and their staff. Right from the top as owner Kirstie took my call while sick at home, to Shalea to Pamela to Jason, to the print shop to... well... EVERYONE. Park Memorial has our deepest thanks and strongest recommendation!"
Nick Fournier
"It was a tough time for our family and the fact that I live in Toronto made things even more difficult."
"This review is long overdue. When my cousin passed away last September, I was in charge of handling funeral planning. It was a tough time for our family and the fact that I live in Toronto made things even more difficult. But Gilla was amazing and really helped the process. I can't say enough. She was extremely patient since I had to relay and explain details to other family members. A big thank you to Gilla and the team!"
John Ly
"It was amazing to have them in our corner making sure this day was what we needed to set us on the path for the healing process that lay ahead."
"When my father passed away in February, the funeral planning seemed daunting at first. All of my worries dissipated one by one with every moment we had speaking with John. It has been almost a month since my dad's funeral, and my mom and I still think about how much genuine kindness, empathy, respect, and care we were shown by not only John, but Casey as well, who was the celebrant recommended by John. I cannot express enough gratitude to both of them for making this day into something so beautiful. It was amazing to have them in our corner making sure this day was what we needed to set us on the path for the healing process that lay ahead. I hope they know how much of an impact they had on my family. They just went above and beyond in every regard and I am forever grateful. It was a day I know my dad would be proud of. If I could give more than 5 stars, I really would."
Sasha Cee
"They guided me and my children every step of the way"
"I had the pleasure of dealing with Alexandra and her team of Professionals at Park Memorial Funeral home after the recent passing of My Wife. They guided me and my children every step of the way through the process of cremation, selecting an urn, Identification and all of the little details of the service. They took care of everything and gave us guidance for all of the things we needed to provide. We are proud to recommend this local business for all of your funeral needs."
Dave Rice
"We were treated extremely well, all our questions answered"
"My husband and daughter and I went in looking for an urn for my father in law and let me tell you how amazing the staff was. We were treated extremely well, all our questions answered, and we were able to take our time and not feel pressured to buy anything right then and there. It was an overall great experience. We did, however walk out with a beautiful urn. Huge thanks to the guys that helped us definitely would give more than just 5 stars if I could."
Robin Andrews
"I hope to not have to do this again anytime soon but I know for sure when the time comes they will be by our side again."
"Dealing with a loss one in the family is never easy. Working with park memorial funeral home they have made the process so easy for our family. Working with Alexandra - she was so amazing. She was caring and compassionate and provided help with all the information not with just the service but with everything else outside the service as well. Our family can never thank her and the people at Park Memorial funeral home enough for everything they did and we will always be forever grateful. I hope to not have to do this again anytime soon but I know for sure when the time comes they will be by our side again."
Steven Nguyen
"The level of care and compassion I received from everyone is very much appreciated and made a horribly traumatizing event as painless as possible."
"Park Memorial was amazing. These people have one of the hardest jobs on the planet. Constantly surrounded by sad people, yet they maintain a loving, caring and respectful demeanour. The level of care and compassion I received from everyone is very much appreciated and made a horribly traumatizing event seamless and as painless as possible. Bless you all and all your hard work."
Jodi Byrne-Marsh
"We had no idea where to go with respect to funeral arrangements but are so happy we picked Park Memorial."
"Back in May 2020 we lost my wife/mother/sister and a friend to many. We had no idea where to go with respect to funeral arrangements but are so happy we picked Park Memorial. I hope we are not in the market to use a funeral home in the near future but if we are…. There really is no choice. Thank you Park Memorial!"
Terry Lashyn
"our staff made an unbearable situation bearable. Your kindness will not be forgotten."
"I cannot say enough about the care and service your Park Memorial Family provides to your clients. We encountered several of your staff while making arrangements, and your staff is truly a Family who work together to provide clients with outstanding service during a very difficult, trying time. Your staff made an unbearable situation bearable. Your kindness will not be forgotten."
Sonia Mudry

Making decisions while bereaved is difficult. We understand.
We have prepared some resources for you to explore that might help to ease the burden of planning a funeral for your loved one.
When a death has occurred:

Our support beyond the funeral:

Why plan ahead?

Services We Provide
List of Services
Planning Ahead
One of the greatest gifts that you can give your family is to preplan your funeral. Prearranging takes the guesswork and often family disagreements, out of funeral planning.
You know that your wishes will be carried out and your loved ones will know exactly how to honour you.
Learn more
List Item  1
Burial
Park Memorial offers a range of burial service choices. These can include simple, immediate burials, graveside services guided by a celebrant or clergy, or a traditional or contemporary funeral service followed by burial.
Our team will guide you through the process of selecting the burial service that best honours your loved one.
Learn more
List Item  2
Cremation
Park Memorial offers a variety of options for families choosing cremation. These include simple, immediate cremation, cremation prior to a memorial service, or cremation following a funeral service.
Graveside or scattering services are also options dependent on your choice of final disposition of your loved one's cremated remains.
Read more
List Item  3
Tributes & Ceremonies
Whether you are planning a traditional funeral, viewing, visitation, a contemporary service, or a celebration of life, we want to help you make the right decisions for you and the family and friends of your loved one.
Your funeral directors will guide you through each step of the process to plan a personalized and meaningful life tribute for your loved one. Park Memorial is proud to serve families of all faiths and cultures. Our funeral directors are trained to plan ceremonies inclusive of all ethnic and religious customs and traditions.
A highly respected Edmonton funeral home with branches serving northern Alberta, Park Memorial gives bereaved families the highest level of professional, empathetic service.
Learn more
List Item  4
Reception Services
Park Memorial offers assistance and planning in organizing a reception in our beautiful Edmonton funeral home facility or at the location of your choice. We offer comprehensive catering options that include buffet or individual boxed lunches.
Read more
Repatriation Services
When a death occurs away from home, our funeral professionals will help arrange the transport of your loved one’s body or cremated remains. Some families choose to transport their loved one back to their homeland for final disposition.
Our team has arranged repatriation of deceased loved ones to countries and continents all over the globe. Each country has its own set of required laws and documents, and our funeral professionals are proficient in helping families with all steps in this process.
Read more
Aftercare
Park Memorial believes that our service to families and to our grieving community needs to continue beyond the funeral service.
We provide both assistance with the many documents and forms that must be filled out when settling an estate, as well as grief support programs. We also offer small group monthly grief support events, as well as annual / biennial large group events that are accessible by the entire community.
Read more

Testimonials of Our Care

"We had nothing but exemplary, compassionate service and guidance from Park Memorial and their staff"


"While my Mother didn't pass away unexpectedly, her end came much more quickly than was expected. We had nothing but exemplary, compassionate service and guidance from Park Memorial (Edmonton) and their staff. Right from the top as owner Kirstie took my call while sick at home, to Shalea to Pamela to Jason, to the print shop to... well... EVERYONE. Park Memorial has our deepest thanks and strongest recommendation!"


Nick Fournier


"It was a tough time for our family and the fact that I live in Toronto made things even more difficult."


"This review is long overdue. When my cousin passed away last September, I was in charge of handling funeral planning. It was a tough time for our family and the fact that I live in Toronto made things even more difficult. But Gilla was amazing and really helped the process. I can't say enough. She was extremely patient since I had to relay and explain details to other family members. A big thank you to Gilla and the team!"


John Ly


"It was amazing to have them in our corner making sure this day was what we needed to set us on the path for the healing process that lay ahead."


"When my father passed away in February, the funeral planning seemed daunting at first. All of my worries dissipated one by one with every moment we had speaking with John. It has been almost a month since my dad's funeral, and my mom and I still think about how much genuine kindness, empathy, respect, and care we were shown by not only John, but Casey as well, who was the celebrant recommended by John. I cannot express enough gratitude to both of them for making this day into something so beautiful. It was amazing to have them in our corner making sure this day was what we needed to set us on the path for the healing process that lay ahead. I hope they know how much of an impact they had on my family. They just went above and beyond in every regard and I am forever grateful. It was a day I know my dad would be proud of. If I could give more than 5 stars, I really would."


Sasha Cee


"They guided me and my children every step of the way"


"I had the pleasure of dealing with Alexandra and her team of Professionals at Park Memorial Funeral home after the recent passing of My Wife. They guided me and my children every step of the way through the process of cremation, selecting an urn, Identification and all of the little details of the service. They took care of everything and gave us guidance for all of the things we needed to provide. We are proud to recommend this local business for all of your funeral needs."


Dave Rice


"We were treated extremely well, all our questions answered"


"My husband and daughter and I went in looking for an urn for my father in law and let me tell you how amazing the staff was. We were treated extremely well, all our questions answered, and we were able to take our time and not feel pressured to buy anything right then and there. It was an overall great experience. We did, however walk out with a beautiful urn. Huge thanks to the guys that helped us definitely would give more than just 5 stars if I could."


Robin Andrews


"I hope to not have to do this again anytime soon but I know for sure when the time comes they will be by our side again."


"Dealing with a loss one in the family is never easy. Working with park memorial funeral home they have made the process so easy for our family. Working with Alexandra - she was so amazing. She was caring and compassionate and provided help with all the information not with just the service but with everything else outside the service as well. Our family can never thank her and the people at Park Memorial funeral home enough for everything they did and we will always be forever grateful. I hope to not have to do this again anytime soon but I know for sure when the time comes they will be by our side again."


Steven Nguyen


"The level of care and compassion I received from everyone is very much appreciated and made a horribly traumatizing event as painless as possible."


"Park Memorial was amazing. These people have one of the hardest jobs on the planet. Constantly surrounded by sad people, yet they maintain a loving, caring and respectful demeanour. The level of care and compassion I received from everyone is very much appreciated and made a horribly traumatizing event seamless and as painless as possible. Bless you all and all your hard work."


Jodi Byrne-Marsh


"We had no idea where to go with respect to funeral arrangements but are so happy we picked Park Memorial."


"Back in May 2020 we lost my wife/mother/sister and a friend to many. We had no idea where to go with respect to funeral arrangements but are so happy we picked Park Memorial. I hope we are not in the market to use a funeral home in the near future but if we are…. There really is no choice. Thank you Park Memorial!"


Terry Lashyn


"our staff made an unbearable situation bearable. Your kindness will not be forgotten."


"I cannot say enough about the care and service your Park Memorial Family provides to your clients. We encountered several of your staff while making arrangements, and your staff is truly a Family who work together to provide clients with outstanding service during a very difficult, trying time. Your staff made an unbearable situation bearable. Your kindness will not be forgotten."


Sonia Mudry

Services We Provide

List of Services

  • Planning Ahead

    One of the greatest gifts that you can give your family is to preplan your funeral. Prearranging takes the guesswork and often family disagreements, out of funeral planning.


    You know that your wishes will be carried out and your loved ones will know exactly how to honour you.

    Learn more List Item 1
  • Burial

    Park Memorial offers a range of burial service choices. These can include simple, immediate burials, graveside services guided by a celebrant or clergy, or a traditional or contemporary funeral service followed by burial. 


    Our team will guide you through the process of selecting the burial service that best honours your loved one.

    Learn more List Item 2
  • Cremation

    Park Memorial offers a variety of options for families choosing cremation. These include simple, immediate cremation, cremation prior to a memorial service, or cremation following a funeral service. 


    Graveside or scattering services are also options dependent on your choice of final disposition of your loved one's cremated remains.

    Read more List Item 3
  • Tributes & Ceremonies

    Whether you are planning a traditional funeral, viewing, visitation, a contemporary service, or a celebration of life, we want to help you make the right decisions for you and the family and friends of your loved one. 


    Your funeral directors will guide you through each step of the process to plan a personalized and meaningful life tribute for your loved one. Park Memorial is proud to serve families of all faiths and cultures. Our funeral directors are trained to plan ceremonies inclusive of all ethnic and religious customs and traditions.


    A highly respected Edmonton funeral home with branches serving northern Alberta, Park Memorial gives bereaved families the highest level of professional, empathetic service.

    Learn more List Item 4
  • Reception Services

    Park Memorial offers assistance and planning in organizing a reception in our beautiful Edmonton funeral home facility or at the location of your choice. We offer comprehensive catering options that include buffet or individual boxed lunches.

    Read more
  • Repatriation Services

    When a death occurs away from home, our funeral professionals will help arrange the transport of your loved one’s body or cremated remains. Some families choose to transport their loved one back to their homeland for final disposition.


    Our team has arranged repatriation of deceased loved ones to countries and continents all over the globe. Each country has its own set of required laws and documents, and our funeral professionals are proficient in helping families with all steps in this process.


    Read more
  • Aftercare

    Park Memorial believes that our service to families and to our grieving community needs to continue beyond the funeral service. 


    We provide both assistance with the many documents and forms that must be filled out when settling an estate, as well as grief support programs. We also offer small group monthly grief support events, as well as annual / biennial large group events that are accessible by the entire community.

    Read more

Services We Provide
List of Services
Planning Ahead
One of the greatest gifts that you can give your family is to preplan your funeral. Prearranging takes the guesswork and often family disagreements, out of funeral planning.
You know that your wishes will be carried out and your loved ones will know exactly how to honour you.
Learn more
List Item  1
Burial
Park Memorial offers a range of burial service choices. These can include simple, immediate burials, graveside services guided by a celebrant or clergy, or a traditional or contemporary funeral service followed by burial.
Our team will guide you through the process of selecting the burial service that best honours your loved one.
Learn more
List Item  2
Cremation
Park Memorial offers a variety of options for families choosing cremation. These include simple, immediate cremation, cremation prior to a memorial service, or cremation following a funeral service.
Graveside or scattering services are also options dependent on your choice of final disposition of your loved one's cremated remains.
Read more
List Item  3
Tributes & Ceremonies
Whether you are planning a traditional funeral, viewing, visitation, a contemporary service, or a celebration of life, we want to help you make the right decisions for you and the family and friends of your loved one.
Your funeral directors will guide you through each step of the process to plan a personalized and meaningful life tribute for your loved one. Park Memorial is proud to serve families of all faiths and cultures. Our funeral directors are trained to plan ceremonies inclusive of all ethnic and religious customs and traditions.
A highly respected Edmonton funeral home with branches serving northern Alberta, Park Memorial gives bereaved families the highest level of professional, empathetic service.
Learn more
List Item  4
Reception Services
Park Memorial offers assistance and planning in organizing a reception in our beautiful Edmonton funeral home facility or at the location of your choice. We offer comprehensive catering options that include buffet or individual boxed lunches.
Read more
Repatriation Services
When a death occurs away from home, our funeral professionals will help arrange the transport of your loved one’s body or cremated remains. Some families choose to transport their loved one back to their homeland for final disposition.
Our team has arranged repatriation of deceased loved ones to countries and continents all over the globe. Each country has its own set of required laws and documents, and our funeral professionals are proficient in helping families with all steps in this process.
Read more
Aftercare
Park Memorial believes that our service to families and to our grieving community needs to continue beyond the funeral service.
We provide both assistance with the many documents and forms that must be filled out when settling an estate, as well as grief support programs. We also offer small group monthly grief support events, as well as annual / biennial large group events that are accessible by the entire community.
Read more

An 80-year-old family-owned and operated funeral home,
devoted to serving your family with care and compassion.
Park Memorial Ltd. is a family owned and operated funeral home with over 80 years of experience serving families from our locations throughout northern Alberta, including
Edmonton
,
Vegreville
,
Mayerthorpe
,
Lamont
, and
Smoky Lake
. We offer a complete selection of traditional and contemporary burial and cremation services and we are proud to honour all cultural and faith-based customs and traditions. Our funeral planning team is among the finest in the profession and their caring attention to detail makes a very difficult and emotional time easier for families.
Testimonials From The Families We Serve
"Park Memorial Funeral Home provides the best service that I can ask for on such a terrible day of losing my grandma and under the strict social restriction due to Covid19. I would like to give my gratitude to Gilla and Jacky Leung for their understanding, professional and helpfulness to my family in this tough time. Gilla and Jacky were easy to connect and always respond to our questions in a timely manner. Gilla and Jacky went out of their way to help my family arranging my grandma's funeral service which made things a lot easier for us during this tough time. Thank you Park Memorial Funeral Home and all the staff for helping us."
Ann Pham
"Back in May 2020 we lost my wife/a mother/sister and a friend to many. We had no idea where to go with respect to funeral arrangements but are so happy we picked Park Memorial. Alexandra from Park Memorial was a kind, considerate and caring person that made the process so much easier. She answered our questions in an extremely timely manner and made us feel like we were the only clients she had. 17 months after the funeral we reached out to Alexandra to help us get some programs printed for the Celebration of Life. She helped us immediately with no questions. I hope we are not in the market to use a funeral home in the near future but if we are… There really is no choice. Thank you Park Memorial!"
Terry Lashyn
"Park Memorial was amazing. These people have one of the hardest jobs on the planet. Constantly surrounded by sad people, yet they maintain a loving, caring and respectful demeanour. My first contact was late evening jan 22 2021. My brother was found deceased in his apartment. They had someone there to collect him in an hour and a half. The 2 gentlemen that picked him up were so kind and thoughtful. I was a complete mess and they reassured me they would take good care of him. Next contact was with Brad. Once again very kind and helpful. We then came in and met with Nicole. She was thoughtful and walked us through my brothers arrangements so throughly still keeping a kind disposition. Then today I received a call my brothers urn was to be picked up. Tracy sat down with me and was so compassionate to our story and even became emotional too, which just showed me how much these people have to endure dealing with grieving people and attempt to not bring that home with them. The level of care and compassion I received from everyone is very much appreciated and made a horribly traumatizing event seamless and as painless as possible. Bless you all and all your hard work. Thank you again."
Jodi Byrne-Marsh
"I cannot say enough about the care and service your Park Memorial Family provides to your clients. I had a very sudden unexpected death of my sister in an Edmonton Hospital a few weeks ago. She was not from Alberta, and her son didn’t make it in time to see her. He was obviously devastated, and wanted to see his mother. It was a Saturday evening, and since I knew of your Funeral home, I called it. I was pleasantly surprised that a real person answered (not answering machine) took our information, said he would arrange to have her picked up, and someone would call first thing in the morning to make arrangements for us to see her. This arrangement was made and we got to spend a couple of hours with her. We were never rushed, Robbi was very kind and caring, and when we were ready, we sat down with her to go through all the logistics, and start arrangement. We soon realized we needed a SIN# which was at her home 1100 km away, and her son had to go back to get it, which paused arrangements. We decided to have a Chapel service for her family here before cremation. Again, Robbi got it organized ,even finding us a Priest to do the service, as we knew nobody here. The two gentlemen attending us at the service (sorry, I do not remember their names) were so compassionate, caring and kind. We encountered several of your staff while making arrangements, and your staff is truly a Family who work together to provide clients with outstanding service during a very difficult, trying time. Your staff made an unbearable situation bearable. Your kindness will not be forgotten. Please pass my sincere Thank You to Robbi and others who attended us."
Sonia Mudry
OUR HERITAGE
The Building of a Dream and a Family
Tod Smolyk started out in 1941 as a funeral director with a dream. He had his own embalming instruments and 12 friends who had each contributed $100 to help him start his company. One of the doors he knocked on introduced Tod to Lucy Kostynuk, who ended up becoming the funeral home’s largest investor. To be able to contribute his share, Tod had to donate his embalming instruments to the company at their appraised value. The courtship of Tod and Lucy turned into an engagement, and the rest was history.
Tod and his fiancée, Lucy, were married at 3 p.m. on November 29, 1941. Instead of heading out to enjoy a honeymoon, they opened the doors to their new funeral home at 6 p.m. that same evening. Park Memorial's first hearse was a 1941 Ford panel truck that was converted locally, and the first car used to chauffeur families was a used Studebaker sedan. Click
here
to learn more about our first steps as a family company.
Tod Smolyk & Lucy (Kostynuk) Smolyk
Park Memorial Founders
1917 - 1976 | 1919- 2002
"I selected the name Park Memorial at a time when all other funeral homes in Edmonton carried the names of their owners. I wanted to ensure there were no overtones suggesting a preference to serve one religious denomination or a specific ethnic group over another." – Tod Smolyk

A Growing Network of Care
As business improved, the company expanded to communities outside of Edmonton. The Vegreville branch was purchased in 1943, the Lamont branch in 1946, the Vilna branch in 1951, the Wildwood and Mayerthorpe branches in 1955, and the Smoky Lake branch in 1956. The present Edmonton building is not the original. The former building was sold and moved off the property and the current building was built in 1963 on the original site of Park Memorial at the corner of 97 Street and 111 Avenue.
The current building was actually built right around the original as it was located on the space that is our front (north) parking lot today. The size of the original 1941 building was much smaller and would have fit entirely in the space occupied by our present chapel.
A Second Generation of Leadership
Jerry Smolyk (In Memorium) & Midge Smolyk
Former President and Second Generation Family Owners
"I love being a funeral director and I am proud to be in funeral service. I see our association
